title: Establish functional color hierarchy and responsive radius presets
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background:
We have accumulated a large number of ad-hoc color and radius tokens over the last two years. This causes inconsistent button/alert/table styles, makes chart palettes hard to reason about, and complicates runtime token resolution for Dedicated/Private deployments. The goal of this ticket is to define a compact, functional color hierarchy and a small set of responsive radius presets that map directly to component roles and interaction states. This is maintenance work: no visual redesign of components, but consolidates tokens so engineering can ship a single token file for hosted/dedicated/private runtimes.

Problem statement:
- Multiple accent and semantic tones exist (accent-01..06, info-weak/strong, success-solid/toned, etc.) with overlapping uses.
- Radius values are inconsistent across controls and break layout parity between compact and comfortable modes.
- Chart palettes leak brand accents and reduce legibility for small-multiple charts.
- Shadow/elevation tokens are applied ad-hoc leading to inconsistent perceived depth.

Proposal summary:
1) Color hierarchy: introduce a role-based palette with three levels per role: base, emphasis, and muted. Roles: neutral, interactive (primary), accent (brand), informational, success, warning, critical. Each role will have tokens named functionally: color.<role>.base, color.<role>.emphasis, color.<role>.muted. Keep the total core swatches under 28 tokens.
2) Contrast targets: enforce AA for normal text and AAA for UI chrome where feasible. Provide contrast-safe aliases: color.text.primary (maps to neutral.emphasis) and color.bg.surface (maps to neutral.base).
3) Chart palettes: introduce a 6-step composable palette (chart.primary[1..6]) with non-saturated midtones plus one high-contrast accent mapped to interactive.emphasis for highlight use. Document fallback order for small multiples.
4) Radius presets: define three responsive radius tokens: radius.compact (4px), radius.default (8px), radius.touch (12px). Components should select radius by breakpoint / density toggle. Provide gesture-aware alias radius.gesture = radius.touch.
5) Elevation tokens: consolidate to elevation.micro, elevation.card, elevation.overlay with shadow specs split into shadow.* tokens (shadow.offset, shadow.blur, shadow.spread, shadow.color) to allow platform-specific synthesis.

Technical notes and constraints:
- Token names must be platform-agnostic (CSS variables, Swift/Android tokens). Keep spec simple to reduce mapping complexity for Private deployments.
- Keep color ramp linear for accessibility checks. Avoid introduction of new color families.
- Provide a migration table from existing tokens to new tokens for automated codemods.

Migration plan (high-level):
- Phase 1 (Design + token definitions): produce canonical token JSON and Figma token styles (this ticket).
- Phase 2 (Engineering integration): ENG implements token aliasing layer; include codemod that updates component imports.
- Phase 3 (Canary rollout): ship to console canary and dedicated small cohort, monitor visual regressions via visual-diff and QA checklist.
- Phase 4 (Default rollout): release tokens as part of console-2026.04 and publish migration guide.

Rollout caveats:
- Some legacy themes used by customers (white-labeled embeds) will need explicit migration; flag these as sub_issues.
- Runtime caching means token name changes must ship with aliasing for at least two releases to avoid flicker in long-lived processes.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- Canonical token JSON (platform-agnostic)
- Figma token styles + prototype pages for buttons, tables, charts
- Migration mapping doc and codemod spec
- Acceptance criteria and QA checklist
acceptance_criteria: Canonical token JSON uploaded to token repo and linked in this ticket
Figma token styles defined and used in 3 representative components (button, small table, stacked bar chart)
Migration mapping sheet completed with one-line mapping for all deprecated tokens
Engineering has an aliasing plan and a codemod spec reviewed by ENG
Accessibility checks: all major UI text contrast meets AA and interactive chrome meets AA (exceptions documented)
Canary rollout plan scheduled with monitoring dashboards and visual-diff tests

comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Patel: Initial triage. Prioritizing consolidation to reduce runtime surface for Private. Assigned to Marco for authoring token JSON.
2026-03-04 - Marco Alvarez: Posted first draft of token JSON to the token repo (link in links). Asked ENG for aliasing constraints; ENG requested kept token count under 32 core tokens.
2026-03-06 - Design review: Feedback from Lina (PM) - prefer 3-step tone per role vs 5-step to reduce cognitive overhead. Agreed and updated spec.

2026-03-09 - Frontend engineering (Nadia Gupta): Confirmed radius.touch=12px is acceptable for mobile gesture targets; requested a 10px intermediate for tablet — added note but holding as future follow-up to avoid scope creep.
2026-03-12 - Marco Alvarez: Uploaded Figma token file v0.3 and created sample pages for buttons/tables/charts. Visual-diff baseline produced for canary. See links.
